source: NCERT Class XI, Performing Arts & Cultural Heritage of India, Ch. 4 (Folk Dances and Folk Music of India).

sections.heading: 1. Folk vs Classical
points: **Folk arts** are the traditional dances and music of ordinary people, tied to **seasons, festivals, harvests, rituals and community life**.
Unlike classical forms, they are **community-based, spontaneous, less codified**, and learnt informally.
They express regional identity and social occasions.

sections.heading: 2. Major Folk Dances by State
points: **Punjab** — **Bhangra** (men, harvest) and **Giddha** (women).
**Gujarat** — **Garba** and **Dandiya Raas** (Navratri).
**Rajasthan** — **Ghoomar, Kalbelia** (snake-charmer community; a UNESCO ICH).
**Maharashtra** — **Lavani**; **Assam** — **Bihu** (spring festival).
**West Bengal** — **Chhau** (also Odisha/Jharkhand; masked, a UNESCO ICH); **Tamil Nadu** — **Karagattam, Kummi**.
**Kerala** — **Theyyam**; **Jammu & Kashmir** — **Rouf**; **Himachal** — **Nati**; **Uttarakhand** — **Chholiya**.

sections.heading: 3. Folk Music and Theatre-linked Forms
points: **Folk music** includes work songs, wedding songs, harvest songs, ballads and devotional songs.
Examples: **Pandavani** (Chhattisgarh — epic narration, Teejan Bai), **Baul** (Bengal — wandering minstrels, a UNESCO ICH), **Powada** (Maharashtra ballads), **Maand** (Rajasthan).
Folk songs are usually in **regional languages/dialects** and passed down orally.

sections.heading: 4. Significance
points: Folk arts preserve **cultural diversity and oral heritage**.
Several are recognised as **UNESCO Intangible Cultural Heritage** (Chhau, Kalbelia, Baul, Ramlila, Kutiyattam).
They strengthen community bonds and mark the rhythm of rural life.

sections.heading: 5. High-Yield One-Liners (Last-Minute Recall)
points: Bhangra/Giddha = Punjab; Garba/Dandiya = Gujarat; Ghoomar/Kalbelia = Rajasthan.
Bihu = Assam; Lavani = Maharashtra; Chhau = Bengal/Odisha/Jharkhand (masked).
Pandavani = Chhattisgarh (Teejan Bai); Baul = Bengal minstrels.
UNESCO ICH: Chhau, Kalbelia, Baul (folk); also Ramlila, Kutiyattam.
Theyyam = Kerala; Rouf = Kashmir.

sections.heading: 6. Common Traps (Watch Out)
points: **Kalbelia (Rajasthan) and Chhau are UNESCO Intangible Cultural Heritage**.
**Bihu = Assam**; **Lavani = Maharashtra**; **Garba = Gujarat**.
**Pandavani (Chhattisgarh)** is associated with **Teejan Bai**.
**Baul** singers are wandering minstrels of **Bengal**.
